A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAST study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original CIFAR and ImageNet classification results, inference measurements, and component ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and adds cyclic-sparsity sensitivity results and training-time and memory measurements.

M1.justification: v4 generalizes Algorithm 1's explicit cosine update to CyclicSchedule, with cosine and triangular schedules evaluated. It also corrects the DyReLU phasing loop to an epoch-range conditional. EAST's three core components remain; the relocated phasing equations and expanded weight-sharing explanation introduce no additional component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet for image classification. The additional sensitivity and resource analyses remain within the existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched benchmark comparisons: SET, RigL, SynFlow, and DCT/DCTpS variants remain as applicable. The new training-cost analysis reuses existing comparators. SRigL, CHT, DSCR, and DynaDiag are added to related-work discussion without reported benchmark evaluations.

E3.justification: Table B.1 changes the EAST CIFAR density multiplier from 3 to 10. v4 also introduces systematic controls over schedule shape, density multiplier, cycle count, and cycle length, plus training-time and memory-estimation protocols. This substantially expands the evaluation design, although the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The limited ResNet-34 cyclic-sparsity study becomes a two-architecture comparison in Figure 6, supplemented by systematic sensitivity tables across both CIFAR datasets and both ResNets in Appendix C. Appendix D adds component-level training-cost and memory analysis. The isolated DyReLU and weight-sharing accuracy ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 gains numerical ± entries, supplementing the previously available shaded variability plots. The new sensitivity tables also report ± values. Both versions already state three CIFAR runs; no increase in repetitions is established, and v4 does not explicitly define the ± quantity.

E6.justification: Table 1 materially revises results: EAST's ResNet-50/CIFAR-100 accuracy at 99.95% changes from 14.23% to 45.55%, while ResNet-34/CIFAR-10 at 99.99% changes from 70.57% to 62.12%. These revisions must be interpreted alongside the changed cyclic setting. Appendix C/D add sensitivity and resource results; main Tables 2–4 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The explicit mathematical definition of the cosine sparsity trajectory in v3 Section 3.3 is removed in favor of a generic schedule function. Other definitions and equations remain, including the phasing mathematics moved from Appendix A.3 to Section 3.1. No actual theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: v4 narrows abstract and introduction claims from significant state-of-the-art improvements and surpassing all tested methods to competitive or improved performance. It also drops the explicit claim to be the first DST method varying both sparsity patterns and levels. The central EAST contribution remains.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly identifies cyclic sparsity as experimental and sensitive to tuning, including configurations that reduce accuracy. It adds architecture-dependent interpretations, practical multiplier/cycle-length guidance, and training-overhead discussion. The central gradient-flow explanation remains, while the unsupported reference to an existing theorem is removed.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link and specifies PyTorch autograd accumulation for shared weights. It documents the new schedule controls and training-cost measurement setup, including A100 hardware, batch size 128 for timing, and torchsummary estimates with batch size 1. Much of the original training recipe is retained.

R1.justification: The DST discussion adds SRigL, CHT, DSCR, and DynaDiag, with new references to Lasby et al. (2024), Wu et al. (2025), and Zhang et al. (2025). The explicit first-DST priority claim is removed, while the broader positioning against sparse-training and extreme-pruning research remains.

P1.justification: Selected abstract, introduction, methodology, and results passages are rewritten, and DyReLU phasing moves from Appendix A.3 into Section 3.1. Author information and citation style change. The main section sequence and much of the explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: The paper switches from two-column to single-column layout with widespread figure and table resizing and relocation. Figure 2 adopts a shared accuracy scale, Figure 6 becomes a three-panel comparison, Table 1 incorporates ± entries, and five appendix tables are added. Appendix tables also reuse main-text table numbers inconsistently with their textual references.

improvement.justification: v4 improves scrutiny of cyclic sparsity through systematic sensitivity results, including adverse configurations, and adds numerical uncertainty, code-access information, and measured training costs. These provide a supported net improvement in transparency and empirical support. The gain is limited by undefined ± notation, inconsistent appendix numbering, and the lack of a clear explanation connecting revised Table 1 scores to the changed density multiplier.
